title: Deep learning models of ultrasonography significantly improved the differential diagnosis performance for superficial soft-tissue masses: a retrospective multicenter study
summary: Ultrasound deep-learning models were evaluated across a training/validation cohort and two hospital test cohorts against pathology-based mass classes and improved radiologist classification.
ai_technology: 1,051 included cases from three hospitals; hospital 1 split train/validation, hospitals 2 and 3 test cohorts; DLM-1 benign/malignant AUC .992 and accuracy .987 in validation; DLM-2 five benign categories; radiologists improved with assistance.

evidence.tested: Ultrasound deep-learning models were evaluated across a training/validation cohort and two hospital test cohorts against pathology-based mass classes and improved radiologist classification.
evidence.unknown: The result is limited to the reported dataset, experimental setting and validation in this study; broader generalization and real-world benefit are not established.
